title: Uncertainty-Calibrated Diffusion for Reliable 3D Molecular Graph Generation

problem.claim: Uncertainty miscalibration can degrade inference and chemical validity in diffusion-based 3D molecular graph generation.

gap.claim: The interaction between epistemic uncertainty from the learned denoiser and aleatoric uncertainty injected during reverse diffusion has been largely overlooked.

contributions.claim: The work analyzes how epistemic uncertainty propagates through diffusion inference and affects sampling quality.
The work proposes UCD, a method that calibrates reverse diffusion to account for epistemic uncertainty.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on standard 3D molecular benchmarks reportedly show improved sampling quality across diverse baseline methods.
The authors report state-of-the-art performance for 3D molecular diffusion.

narrative_sequence.summary: Bayesian inference models epistemic uncertainty through predictive distributions.
Uncertainty miscalibration creates difficulties for diffusion-based 3D molecular graph generation under chemical constraints.
The interaction between epistemic and reverse-diffusion aleatoric uncertainty can inflate variance and distort the simulated distribution.
The work studies uncertainty propagation and its effect on sampling quality.
The authors introduce UCD and report benchmark improvements.

source_observation.claim: Epistemic uncertainty from the denoiser can interact with intentionally injected diffusion noise.

interpretation.claim: Uncertainty sources should be analyzed jointly when they accumulate across an inference process.

application.claim: Calibrate iterative generative inference to account for model uncertainty in addition to process noise.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this principle transfers beyond 3D molecular diffusion.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the benchmark datasets, evaluation metrics, or baseline methods.
The calibration procedure and theoretical assumptions are not described.
Independent verification, ablations, limitations, and failure cases are not reported.
